extracted.intended_audience: authors of research software preparing submissions to JOSS (research software developers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting a short research-software paper and associated software repository to the Journal of Open Source Software (JOSS), including required repository, licensing, authorship, paper content, and review-process expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open-source licensing (OSI definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The software should be open source as per the OSI definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an OSI-approved open source license in the repository. This is a precondition for submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obvious research application
rubrics_metrics.description: The software should have an obvious research application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JOSS publishes articles about research software that: solves complex modeling problems in scientific contexts; supports research instruments or experiments; extracts knowledge from large data sets; offers mathematical libraries; or similar research-oriented functionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship: major contribution requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You should be a major contributor to the software you are submitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purely financial or organizational contributions are not sufficient for co-authorship; active project direction and non-code contributions are acceptable. Co-authors must agree to be listed and be accountable for the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance to research software ecosystem
rubrics_metrics.description: The software should be a significant contribution to the available open source software, enabling new research challenges or making research substantially easier/better.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: enabling new research questions, improving speed/ease/simplicity of addressing research challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature-completeness and maintainability
rubrics_metrics.description: The software should be feature-complete (no half-baked solutions) and designed for maintainable extension (not one-off modifications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions that are incomplete prototypes or one-off hacks are discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of minor utility/thin API packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Minor 'utility' packages, including 'thin' API clients, are not acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Packages that do not represent a substantive, research-enabling contribution should not be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository hosting of paper and materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Your paper (paper.md and BibTeX files, plus any figures) must be hosted in a Git-based repository, ideally together with your software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a Git-hosting service (GitHub, Bitbucket, etc.) and place paper.md, paper.bib, and figure files in the repository.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository must be clonable without registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The software must be stored in a repository that can be cloned without registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure public clone access so reviewers can fetch the code without having to sign in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository must be browsable without registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The repository should be browsable online without registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code browsing/viewing should not require a login.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue tracker must be readable without registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The repository must have an issue tracker that is readable without registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers and readers should be able to view past issues/communication publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository must permit filing issues
rubrics_metrics.description: The repository must permit individuals to create issues/file tickets against your repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure external users can open issues so reviewers can request fixes/questions or users can report bugs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-submission availability and license
rubrics_metrics.description: Before you submit, make your software available in an open repository and include an OSI-approved open source license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare the repository, license, and public access prior to starting the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformity to JOSS review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure that the software complies with the JOSS review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In particular, your software should be full-featured, well-documented, and contain procedures (such as automated tests) for checking correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper format and filename
rubrics_metrics.description: Write a short paper in Markdown format using paper.md as the file name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the provided example paper to match correct format and include required sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper components: metadata and minimal sections
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper should contain limited metadata: title, summary, author names, affiliations, and key references. Include Statement of Need, Summary, Acknowledgements, and References sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include full API documentation or extensive software docs in the paper; these belong in the software documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary for a non-specialist
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin the paper with a summary of the high-level functionality of your software for a non-specialist reader. Avoid jargon in this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include sentences that explain software functionality and domain of use to a diverse, non-specialist audience and explicitly explain research applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper length constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper should be between 250 and 1000 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JOSS papers are short by design; 'full length' papers are not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Need
rubrics_metrics.description: A clear Statement of Need must be included that illustrates the research purpose of the software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe why this software is needed in the research context and what gap it fills.

rubrics_metrics.name: References and citation format
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a list of key references, including references to other software addressing related needs; citations should be in rMarkdown format and built from a .bib file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use paper.bib and rMarkdown citation syntax (e.g., @author:2001) so references are generated automatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mention of research projects/publications enabled
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention (if applicable) any past or ongoing research projects using the software and recent scholarly publications enabled by it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This contextualizes the software's research impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of financial support
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge any financial support in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include funding acknowledgements in the Acknowledgements section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of paper and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Software documentation such as API functionality should not be included in the paper and instead should be outlined in the software documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the paper focused and short; link to or point readers to the software docs for API details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission involves filling in the short submission form and waiting for the managing editor to start a pre-review issue in the JOSS reviews repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After submission the managing editor will create a pre-review issue; further review proceeds from there.

rubrics_metrics.name: No submission fees
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no fees for submitting or publishing in JOSS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JOSS's cost model is public; authors should not expect to pay submission/publication fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are welcome to submit their papers to a preprint server at any point; submission to a preprint server is not considered previous publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: arXiv, bioRxiv, SocArXiv, PsyArXiv, etc. are acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship accountability and post-publication correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-authors must agree to be listed and be accountable for all aspects of the work and must notify JOSS if any retraction or correction is needed after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that all listed authors understand and accept responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proprietary languages/dev environments policy
rubrics_metrics.description: JOSS strongly prefers software that doesn’t rely upon proprietary development environments/programming languages, but will consider submissions using proprietary tools if they meet requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If accepted, authors may be asked to help find reviewers who already have the required development environment installed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public review process and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews are public and carried out in a GitHub issue in the JOSS reviews repository with two or more reviewers assigned by the handling editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors will respond to reviewer-raised issues on the submission repository’s issue tracker. Reviewer and editor contributions should be acknowledged in the repository.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-review release and archiving requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon successful completion of the review, authors must make a tagged release of the software and deposit a copy of the repository with a data-archiving service (e.g., Zenodo or figshare), obtain a DOI, and update the review issue thread with the version number and DOI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After JOSS assigns a DOI for the accepted paper, metadata is deposited with CrossRef and listed on the JOSS website; the review issue will be closed and an automatic tweet will announce it.
